title: "Throw Over the Wall" Dependency Releases
pattern: Publishing an internal utility as an open-source dependency without a dedicated mandate or plan to support portability across external platforms.
why_bad: It creates a disconnected fork, making it impossible to reincorporate external bug fixes into the original codebase and damaging the organization's reputation.
detection: OSS projects published by the organization that lack CI testing across target platforms or have unresolved public bug reports.
counterexample: Releasing self-contained documentation or static templates that carry no maintenance burden.
fix: Establish a clear ownership plan and compatibility guarantees before open-sourcing any codebase.
source: *Software Engineering at Google (Winters et al.), Chapter 21, p. 452 [188-191, 660]*
